title: City Sightseeing
goal: Ask about an attraction, choose an admission option, and follow a short sightseeing explanation.

runs.text: Admission
means entry to a place or event; an
admission fee
is its entry price. A
guided tour
is led by a guide. An
audio guide
provides recorded information. A
visitor center
or
tourist information office
provides local information.
Souvenir
means an item kept as a reminder of a place or experience.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: What time does the museum open?

turns.en: What time does the museum open?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Ten today. The last entry is at four thirty.

turns.en: Ten today. The last entry is at four thirty.

runs.text: And when does it close?
Five.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Is there a guided tour this afternoon?

turns.en: Is there a guided tour this afternoon?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: At one and three. Admission and the tour are separate tickets.

turns.en: At one and three. Admission and the tour are separate tickets.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: How much would both cost for one adult?

turns.en: How much would both cost for one adult?

runs.text: Last entry

is the final time visitors are admitted; it can differ from closing time. Ask “Is the audio guide included?” rather than assuming it is. “Is there a step-free entrance?” asks about a specific access feature. You can follow up with “Which entrance should I use?” or “Could you tell me about the route inside?”
Fictional museum card: adult admission $12; tour $5 extra; audio guide $3; opens 10:00; last entry 4:30; closes 5:00; tours at 1:00 and 3:00; step-free entry at the garden entrance.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: I'd like one admission ticket and the three o'clock tour.

turns.en: I'd like one admission ticket and the three o'clock tour.

runs.text: That's seventeen dollars.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Thanks. Where does the tour meet?

turns.en: Thanks. Where does the tour meet?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: By the information desk, ten minutes before it starts.

turns.en: By the information desk, ten minutes before it starts.

blocks.caption: Choose, or decide against it · Visitor & Employee

runs.text: “I'm just looking at the options” postpones a purchase. “That's more than I wanted to spend” states a budget concern. “We'll come back another day” changes the plan. A friendly offer is not an obligation to buy.
A tour guide may say “On your right is the old courthouse” or “Across from it is the public garden.” On a
tour bus
, these expressions describe your current viewpoint. Check a location if you lose track: “Do you mean the building with the clock?”

turns.speaker: Guide

runs.text: On your left is the Harbor Gallery. The visitor center is next to it.

turns.en: On your left is the Harbor Gallery. The visitor center is next to it.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Is the market behind the gallery?

turns.en: Is the market behind the gallery?

turns.speaker: Guide

runs.text: Yes, and the gardens are across the street.

turns.en: Yes, and the gardens are across the street.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Great. Is there time to visit the market after the tour?

turns.en: Great. Is there time to visit the market after the tour?

turns.speaker: Guide

runs.text: It closes at six in this itinerary.

turns.en: It closes at six in this itinerary.

blocks.caption: Talk about what you see · Guide & Visitor

runs.text: The landmarks and timetable are fictional. A
map
or
guidebook
can help you point to a place; you can ask for one instead of pretending you have it.
Use the museum card. Ask about last entry, the three o'clock tour, and the combined adult price. Partner supplies the card's details.
You want the step-free entrance. Ask where it is and what else you need to know. Partner answers “The garden entrance,” then offers to explain the inside route.
Rehearse the short guide exchange. With the model hidden, tell a companion where the market and gardens are relative to the gallery.
Change your budget: you only want admission. State that choice without apologizing for it.
Alone, read the employee's answers and create your visitor turns; then describe the fictional landmarks out loud.
Possibilities:

“Is four thirty the closing time or the last entry?” “Just admission, please.” “The market is behind the gallery.” Check that the ticket, time, access question, and landmark relationship are clear. Directions receive fuller practice in Chapter 78.

ja: 入場・見学・目の前の場所。
note: 開館時刻と最終入場は別です。見学を選ぶ前に、料金と時間を確認し、案内の位置関係を聞き取ります。
